Subject: GPU Roster Gap Analysis — MosaicAI Q4 Ramp

Hi Ben / Aditya,

Shortcut: MosaicAI (Sara Jensen) just sent final growth numbers for their Q4 ramp. They want a 12-month reserved commitment starting Oct 1 (deal MSA-78321) but will have a 6-week burst window during initial product launch where they estimate 180–220 A100-equivalent GPU peak and roughly 100–130 steady-state thereafter. I attached Mosaic's capacity request PDF for context.

High-level asks for ops:
- Can you run a roster/availability check for Oct–Dec (calendar Q4) and a nearby 6-week surge window?
- Where are the feasible pools (us-west-2 vs us-east-1)? Any maintenance or capacity fragmentation concerns?
- What minimal soft-hold would we need to block to make the sales commitment credible while we get procurement signed? (happy path: soft hold that can be released if DocuSign stalls)

Mosaic is sensitive to latency; they want multi-region redundancy but will prioritize us-west if needed. Karthik, I looped you so we can be transparent with Sara on what we can provision ahead of DocuSign.

Thanks — Marissa

Subject: Re: GPU Roster Gap Analysis — MosaicAI Q4 Ramp

Marissa — quick inventory snapshot and recommendation attached (roster_snapshot_q3.csv). Summary:

- Current free pool (uncommitted) across regions for Oct–Dec: ~90 A100-equivalent GPUs (us-west-2: 50, us-east-1: 40).
- Committed reservations (existing Dedicated): ~120 GPUs already spoken for across other deals during Q4 (not available for new holds).
- Short-term slack (due to maintenance and scheduled node ops): ~10–15% of each pool may be unavailable for short windows — most notable week-of-Nov-12 where we have a cross-region reimage.
- Fragmentation: several reservations are per-GPU-type and per-instance; we can re-pack some workloads but nontrivial coordination will be required if we move customers.

Recommendation:
- Place a provisional soft-hold of 60 GPUs today (expires 2028-09-15) distributed: us-west-2 => 40, us-east-1 => 20. This protects a credible steady-state footprint and gives us runway to finish DocuSign.
- For the expected 6-week peak (180–220), propose an "ops-bridge" plan: enable workload-quantization/int8 path which could reduce A100-equivalent needs by ~25–30% if Mosaic accepts a slight perf variance. That would reduce peak from 220 to ~155 equivalent.
- If Mosaic insists on non-quantized capacity for the full peak, we need to negotiate a firm reserve (120 GPUs) or coordinate short-term burst credits with cloud partners — both are slower.

Attachments: roster_snapshot_q3.csv (attachment)

If you want I can open a provisional ticket and set the soft-hold today; need written confirmation on expected start window from Mosaic to justify.

Ben

--
Ben Carter

ben.carter@redwood.com

Sara / Marissa — looping in Mosaic's ask. Per our commercial terms (MSA-78321), Mosaic has a 12-month reserved commitment (starts Oct 1) for 100 reserved units. The launch plan includes an initial product push that could temporarily require 180–220 units for 4–6 weeks while customer acquisition spikes. Procurement is on a tight timeline — Mosaic's finance would like an indication from Redwood on provisional capacity to show to their procurement team.

Ben, excerpting your note:
> Current free pool (uncommitted) across regions for Oct–Dec: ~90 A100-equivalent GPUs (us-west-2: 50, us-east-1: 40).
> Recommendation: Place a provisional soft-hold of 60 GPUs today (expires 2028-09-15) distributed: us-west-2 => 40, us-east-1 => 20.

Sara — would a provisional 60-GPU soft-hold meet Mosaic's procurement needs while legal and procurement finish signatures? If so, we can capture that as an agreed pre-sign commitment and document it in HubSpot and the deal playbook. Alternatively, if Mosaic needs stronger assurance for the 6-week peak, please indicate whether quantization is acceptable (reduces GPU need ~25%).

DocuSign link for the signed SOW will be shared once legal finishes the last redlines.

Thanks — Karthik

Thanks everyone — aligned summary and next steps: 

1) Soft-hold: Ops to place a provisional soft-hold of 60 A100-equivalent GPUs today (placed as an ops-only hold that does not appear as a billing reservation) with automatic expiry on 2028-09-15 unless extended by written confirmation. Distribution: us-west-2 = 40, us-east-1 = 20. Ben, please confirm the ticket ID once created.

2) Surge strategy: If Mosaic accepts quantization for the initial peak, we treat the peak as manageable via runtime optimizations and short-term burst capacity. If they require no quantization, we escalate to Partnerships for cloud-burst credits or require a firm reserved commitment in the SOW.

3) Documentation / CRM: Karthik, please add the provisional hold note to HubSpot (company record linked) and attach the mosaic_capacity_request.pdf. Related HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

4) Ops sync: Schedule a 30-minute ops-sync for Mon, Jul 30, 10:00 PDT to walk through reimage windows, maintenance impacts, and the hold release process. Aditya / Grace — please make the ops checklist (ops-action-items.md) and share a read-only link to the deal folder.

Sara — appreciate if you can confirm (A) whether a 60-GPU provisional hold is sufficient for Mosaic's procurement team, and (B) whether quantization is an acceptable mitigation for the surge. That confirmation will let us decide whether to pursue cloud-burst credits or to push for a firm reserve in DocuSign.

Marissa
